parsed.explanation: No trans-specific criminal offence or documented visitor-facing border/facility restriction; anti-discrimination and hate-speech law cover gender identity, relationships are legally recognised, and the state secured a maximum 30-year sentence for the 2022 Pride mass shooting. Offsetting negatives: reported anti-LGBT hate crime rose 18% in 2023, clearance fell to 45%, only 8% of victims report, and fringe anti-trans mobilisation plus online threats persist. No evidence addresses border screening, custody, facilities, or visitor care. Resident gender-affirming care is narrow but is a climate signal, not a visitor rule. The rating reflects a liberal protective regime with real recourse gaps and isolated severe violence, not state targeting.

entry_documents.protection: Not documented. National self-declaration does not establish foreign-passport or border treatment.
entry_documents.interaction: No evidence on entry screening, marker mismatch, or detention referral.

investigation_detention_custody.exposure: Anti-LGBT hate-crime reports rose; clearance fell from 52% to 45% with more cases dropped; only 8% of victims report, many citing dismissive treatment.
investigation_detention_custody.protection: Hate-crime framework covers gender identity and expression; dedicated reporting group exists; Pride shooter sentenced to 30 years.
investigation_detention_custody.interaction: Serious cases can be prosecuted, but routine recourse is weakened by low reporting and clearance.

federal_state_facilities.exposure: The dossier does not document bathroom, changing-room, custody, or detention placement rules for trans visitors.
federal_state_facilities.protection: Anti-discrimination law covers gender identity and expression in services, but facility access is not specified.
federal_state_facilities.interaction: No documented interaction with border or custody because practices are absent from the record.

care_services.exposure: Resident gender-affirming care is narrow (about one in four referrals; non-binary treatment absent as of 2023); visitor HRT and care access are not documented.
care_services.protection: 2020 guideline states informed consent and no psychiatric precondition; conversion therapy is banned; service anti-discrimination applies.
care_services.interaction: A visitor needing continuity of care faces uncertainty, but no medication seizure or care-denial incident is documented.

threat_framing_law_enforcement.exposure: Anti-trans hostility is documented mainly among far-right and religious fundamentalists and some anti-trans feminist groups; online threats and a drag event were targeted.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.protection: No trans-specific offence; hate speech covers gender identity; the prime minister and state bodies condemn anti-trans hate; security service reports declining threats.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.interaction: The state is not threat-framing; hostile actors are fringe, but online intimidation and Pride-period risk remain.

minors_guardians.exposure: Resident minors face parental joint application for legal gender change ages 6-16, restrictions under 6, and under-18 care only via national service assessment; visitor-minor exposures are not documented.
minors_guardians.protection: Parental-consent route and municipal supportive counselling exist for residents; no visitor-specific protection is documented.
minors_guardians.interaction: A trans minor travelling with a guardian has no documented border or facility barrier, but care access is uncertain.

street_violence_police_response.exposure: 2022 Pride mass shooting; knife attack investigated as a hate crime; online threats against a drag event; reported hate crimes rose 18% in 2023.
street_violence_police_response.protection: Pride shooter received the maximum 30-year sentence; hate-crime framework and police reporting unit operate; security service reports declining threats.
street_violence_police_response.interaction: State response to severe violence is strong, but clearance and reporting gaps leave lower-level harassment under-remedied.

remedies_unknowns.exposure: Low trust, dropped cases, and official undercount; no data on border screening, custody, facilities, or visitor care.
remedies_unknowns.protection: Anti-discrimination statute, hate-speech law, hate-crime counting, and courts provide formal remedies.
remedies_unknowns.interaction: Formal protections exist, but practical remedy for hate crime is uneven; unknowns are not treated as safety.

anchor_checks.comparison: Similar legal equality and anti-discrimination, but this dossier documents rising hate crime, falling clearance to 45%, only 8% reporting, and a Pride mass shooting; remedies are less consistently shown to work, so it sits below 0.85-A.

This jurisdiction has stronger anti-discrimination and hate-crime law and a prosecuted mass shooter, with no documented border detention practice; but serious violence and weak clearance/reporting keep it only slightly above 0.75-C, not at 0.85.

Unlike 0.55-B's discretionary border exclusion and administrative return risk, this dossier shows no trans-specific criminalisation or entry restriction, plus self-declaration and anti-discrimination protection; it is clearly safer than the 0.55 tier.

parsed.synthesis: The operative regime is national and protective: no trans-specific criminal offence, hate-speech and anti-discrimination law covering gender identity and expression, legal relationship recognition, and a strong state response to the Pride shooting. The main documented exposure is societal hate crime and online intimidation, aggravated by low reporting (8%) and falling clearance (45%), so recourse is real but uneven. Anti-trans organising is fringe and condemned by officials, and the security service reports declining threats. Border, custody, facilities, and visitor-care practice are undocumented; under the rubric that is not safety, but no traveller-facing restriction is shown. Resident gender-affirming care restrictions are a climate signal, not a visitor rule. The result is low risk but not flawless, below the strongest protective anchors because of current hate-crime trends and enforcement gaps.
